source.title: A Convergence Theory for Deep Learning via Over-Parameterization
source.authors: Zeyuan Allen-Zhu; Yuanzhi Li; Zhao Song

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices and figure captions.
record.tranche_reason: The paper proves convergence on non-degenerate training data and gives a small empirical illustration with 20% label noise. It does not test completely random labels, shuffled inputs, or generalization under random labels; the theory is an optimization result rather than a reproduction of the original memorization experiments.
record.gate_note: The CIFAR-10 noisy-label figures report training-objective landscapes, not training error, test error, or fitting random labels. Theoretical convergence results concern arbitrary labels only under a pairwise-distinct-input assumption, not completely random relabeling specifically. Cited findings are excluded.
record.test_reason: The convergence guarantees allow arbitrary bounded labels on pairwise-distinct inputs, so they cover completely random labels as a mathematical special case. This bears on V1's fitting component despite the absence of a random-label experiment. The guarantees also cover distinct unstructured inputs under the stated assumptions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly correct. The authors prove polynomial-time fitting guarantees for sufficiently over-parameterized networks on separated inputs, including perfect classification training accuracy, without requiring meaningful labels or structured inputs. They acknowledge that the polynomial requirements may be impractical and do not explicitly analyze test generalization.
record.recipe_differences: The main contribution is a convergence proof for over-parameterized networks, with limited training-landscape illustrations; it does not reproduce the random-label memorization intervention and measurements in the original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: The illustrative plots use CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and 20%-noisy CIFAR-10 across VGG19, ResNet-32, and ResNet-110 architectures; for the stated trajectory setup, learning rate changes at epochs 81 and 122.

fits_no_version.finding: Objective landscapes and gradient norms are illustrated during training on clean and 20%-noisy CIFAR-10.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Negative gradient directions can decrease the training objective along the illustrated SGD trajectories.

record.problems: The theoretical results are convergence guarantees under stated assumptions, not experiments on random labels or test generalization. The noisy-label illustrations are figure-only and do not state training error or test error; the stated empirical setup is limited to 20% noise.
record.rows_left_out: No other claim-relevant numerical outcomes were reported. Figures 1–4 compare clean CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 landscapes; they do not measure the listed claim versions. The text does not provide extractable numerical values from Figures 5–7.

untested.parts: Chance test error and empirical fitting by practical standard networks with unchanged training settings. The theoretical width and learning-rate requirements may be far outside practical regimes.
A small constant-factor training-time difference between true and random labels, and slowing with increasing corruption. A uniform polynomial upper bound does not establish either comparison.
Explicit experiments on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian noise using the original practical networks and settings.
The joint empirical corruption sweep showing perfect training fit and steadily worsening test error. The theory supplies no test-error trajectory.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on random-label fitting, and generalization after removing regularization.
Learning shared real-data patterns before memorizing noise.

missing.what: A theoretical-result row recording arbitrary-label fitting on separated inputs: perfect classification training accuracy and arbitrarily small regression loss under sufficient polynomial width. Random labels and distinct unstructured inputs are included by the assumptions, rather than separately demonstrated experimentally.
missing.locator: Assumption 2.1; Theorems 1–2 and 6–8; Section 6; Appendix A.

record.verdict_notes: The record incorrectly excludes the theoretical fitting guarantees merely because random labels were not separately instantiated. Universal guarantees can bear on these versions. They do not establish practical unchanged-setting performance or relative optimization speed.

versions.untested_parts: No experiment or theorem specifically tests completely random labeling, chance test error, or fitting without changing training settings.
No comparison of training time for true versus random labels or sweep over corruption fractions.
No shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
The figures include 20% label noise but do not report perfect training fit or test error across a corruption sweep.
No comparison of regularization or data augmentation on random-label fitting or true-label generalization.
No measurement of learning order or comparison between learning real patterns and memorizing noise.
